pull.title: ci: Share qa-assets across GitHub Actions jobs
pull.body:
CI jobs download the same qa-assets inputs separately. As reported in #36814, these repeated requests can fail with HTTP 504 before the tests start.

Add one preparation job that checks out qa-assets once per workflow run and shares the unit-test data and fuzz corpus through Actions artifacts. Linux, macOS and Windows consumers verify the selected revision and file hashes before using them.

Containers mount the shared inputs read-only. Fuzz jobs use separate writable copies. Standalone CI scripts keep direct acquisition through the common download helper.

ci: Share qa-assets across GitHub Actions jobs

Acquire qa-assets once per workflow run and distribute verified unit
vectors and fuzz inputs through same-run artifacts. Reuse the common
helper for Linux, macOS and Windows consumers instead of downloading the
same inputs in each job.

Package the inputs as tar files so the artifact downloader extracts one
file instead of many small corpus files. Let artifact ZIP compression
handle the transfer and extract the tar before verification.

Record the selected revision and file hashes, mount shared inputs
read-only in containers, and give fuzz jobs separate writable copies.
Keep standalone acquisition and select a fresh snapshot each run.

Refs https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36814.

events.body:
thx for working on this, but this is adding ~300 loc, which need to be reviewed, tested, and maintained (as they can contain bugs or require other changes in the future).

IIUC the issue they are trying to fix happened in two pull requests over the last year? It would be good to get an idea of how often this will fix an issue, so that it is clear that the time spent reviewing/maintaining this every year is less than the time it takes to click the re-run CI button every year.

On could also cache other stuff, like https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/33913#issue-3646740449, but this hasn't been done yet either, because it is not worth it.

It just depends how much importance one gives to determinism in tests. Obviously for a cryptographer's mind this is of paramount importance. Failing tests may also drive wrong decision making, re-runs feel like... switch it off and on again, see if that works 😅

Generally, the tests aren't meant to be 100% deterministic, but rather reproducible, so that failures are actionable. For example, the functional and unit tests can take a random seed, which is logged, for a bit of "property-based" testing. On any test failure, one should trivially see all the actions and inputs that lead to the failure and reproduce the exact failure.

The tests itself should never have any network access (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31349), so network io errors can only happen during CI runs. Those can happen in many different places: docker image cache, docker volume cache, package manager downloads, other dependency downloads, `depends` downloads, previous-release bin downloads, unit test assets, fuzz test assets, ...

Every week there are a few of those network failures, which is extremely annoying, but at the same time something that can't really be fixed: If a cache is created for one resource, then creating the cache can still fail, or downloading the cache itself may fail instead. Also, spotting network failures is generally easier to deal with than a real intermittent ci failure or some of the failures caused by corrupt VM hardware. See https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues?q=is%3Aissue+state%3Aclosed+label%3A%22CI+failed%22

See e.g:

```
toomanyrequests: Quota exceeded for quota metric 'Requests per project in the US multi-region' and limit 'Requests per project in the US multi-region per minute' of service 'artifactregistry.googleapis.com' for consumer 'project_number:342927644502'.
```

https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/45420610531/job/138538761564?pr=36966#step:11:172

And an apt error earlier today, ...
